# qunix

> An educational x86_64 macrokernel (monolithic kernel) written from scratch in Rust. It exists to
> document two things with evidence: where Rust stops helping when you are implementing the very
> abstractions it protects you with, and where AI-assisted development stops helping when a
> plausible, compiling, passing answer can still be wrong in a way nothing reports.

qunix boots UEFI via Limine, runs preemptive kernel threads across isolated address spaces, brings
every application processor online, and enters ring 3 through its own SYSCALL/SYSRET ABI. It is a
research kernel: no filesystem, no driver model, no network stack, no stable ABI.

Key findings, stated plainly:

- Rust did not prevent this project's memory-corruption bugs. Every one lived inside an `unsafe`
  block carrying a comment that explained why it was sound. What Rust bought was locality: the
  search space was a handful of functions rather than the whole kernel.
- The failure mode of AI-assisted systems programming is plausibility, not incompetence. Code that
  compiles, matches idiom, carries a confident safety comment, and passes tests it also wrote.
- Allocators do not crash when they are wrong. Fuzzing found real corruption only once the harness
  stopped looking for panics and asserted that no two live allocations overlap.
- A fuzz target that normalises its inputs cannot find bugs in the normalisation.

## Pages

- [Overview](https://quinnjr.github.io/qunix/): what exists, the honest position on Rust, and the
  three defects that justified the project.
- [Design decisions](https://quinnjr.github.io/qunix/design/): every non-obvious architectural
  choice with the constraint that produced it — buddy allocator, slab heap, per-CPU state through
  GS, SMP bring-up, preemption ordering rules, owned address spaces, SYSCALL ABI, W^X.
- [vs Linux / OpenBSD / Redox](https://quinnjr.github.io/qunix/comparisons/): where qunix diverges
  from each and why, including where the established systems are simply right.
- [AI-assisted development](https://quinnjr.github.io/qunix/ai/): the evidence-based account — what
  worked, the specific bugs produced, why review missed them, and the three practices that caught
  them.
